summary: This bill modifies the tax exclusion for capital gains from qualified small business stock by gradually increasing the exclusion percentage based on how long the stock is held, reducing the minimum holding period from five to three years, and expanding eligibility to include S corporations and certain convertible debt instruments.

scores.thoughts: This bill modifies the exclusion for gain from qualified small business stock, expanding the applicable percentage of gain that can be excluded and shortening the required holding period. This effectively lowers the tax burden on certain capital gains, thus reducing taxes for qualifying individuals and businesses.

The bill expands the Section 1202 capital-gains exclusion for qualified small-business stock by lowering the holding period, raising the exclusion percentages, and extending eligibility to S corporations and convertible debt. These changes reduce federal tax revenue with no offsetting revenue provisions, thereby increasing the deficit to support small-business investment.
